brief.use_case: Assess whether a home is safe for a walker user discharged after hip replacement
brief.guideline:
Home Safety Check: Stairs and Bathroom
Adapted from CDC STEADI 'Check for Safety' (public domain)

STAIRS AND STEPS
- Nothing should be left on the steps: pick up shoes, books, bags and anything else you could trip on.
- Any step that is broken, loose or uneven must be repaired.
- There should be a light over the staircase, with a switch you can reach at the top and at the bottom.
- Handrails should be firmly attached on both sides of the stairs and run the whole length of the stairway.
- Carpet on the stairs must be tight to every step; remove it or tack it down if it is loose or torn.

BATHROOM
- The floor of the tub or shower needs a non-slip mat or adhesive safety strips.
- Grab bars should be installed inside the tub or shower and beside the toilet to help you get in, out, up and down.
- Small bath rugs that slide or have curled edges should be removed, or replaced with rugs that have a non-skid backing.
- Keep a night light on so the path to the bathroom is visible at night.
- A raised toilet seat or a toilet safety frame makes it easier to sit and stand, especially after hip surgery.

row.name: Objects left on stairs
row.visual_description: Shoes, books, bags, or other items resting on stair treads.
recommended_fix: Remove all objects from stairs and store elsewhere
row.post_op_modifier: A walker user cannot step around clutter and is at high risk of catastrophic fall on stairs.
row.citation: Nothing should be left on the steps: pick up shoes, books, bags and anything else you could trip on.

row.name: No grab bar at tub/shower
row.visual_description: Tub or shower wall shows no anchored grab bar for entry, exit, up/down movement.
detection_cues: only tile or glass visible at grab height
recommended_fix: Install ADA-height grab bar inside tub/shower
row.post_op_modifier: Walker users after hip replacement cannot use the walker inside the tub, making a grab bar essential for safe transfers.
row.citation: Grab bars should be installed inside the tub or shower and beside the toilet to help you get in, out, up and down.

row.name: Broken or uneven steps
row.visual_description: Cracked, splintered, sagging, or unevenly spaced stair treads visible in the staircase.
detection_cues: visible crack or hole in tread
recommended_fix: Repair or replace damaged steps before use
row.post_op_modifier: Uneven footing is especially dangerous for a walker user with limited hip flexion and weight-bearing restrictions.
row.citation: Any step that is broken, loose or uneven must be repaired.

row.name: No support at toilet
row.visual_description: Wall or floor area beside toilet shows no grab bar or toilet safety frame mounted.
recommended_fix: Install grab bar or toilet safety frame beside toilet
row.post_op_modifier: Sitting/standing motions are high-risk for hip precautions; lack of support increases fall and dislocation risk.
row.citation: Grab bars should be installed inside the tub or shower and beside the toilet to help you get in, out, up and down.

row.name: Missing or inaccessible stair lighting
row.visual_description: No visible light fixture over the staircase, or light switch not visible/reachable at top or bottom of stairs.
detection_cues: single switch only at one end
recommended_fix: Install overhead light with switches at both top and bottom
row.post_op_modifier: Poor visibility increases misstep risk for a walker user who already has reduced balance reserve.
row.citation: There should be a light over the staircase, with a switch you can reach at the top and at the bottom.

row.name: Slippery tub/shower floor
row.visual_description: Tub or shower floor surface appears smooth/glossy with no mat or textured strips visible.
recommended_fix: Add non-slip mat or adhesive safety strips to tub/shower floor
row.post_op_modifier: Reduced balance and weight-bearing restrictions after hip surgery make slick surfaces especially dangerous with a walker nearby.
row.citation: The floor of the tub or shower needs a non-slip mat or adhesive safety strips.

row.name: Handrail missing on one side of stairs
row.visual_description: Only one side of the staircase has a handrail, or a rail is absent for part of the run.
detection_cues: rail present only on one side
gap in railing along the run
recommended_fix: Install handrail on both sides for full length of stairway
row.post_op_modifier: A walker user relies on bilateral rail support for sit-to-stand and stair negotiation post-hip-replacement.
row.citation: Handrails should be firmly attached on both sides of the stairs and run the whole length of the stairway.

row.name: Loose bath mat or rug on bathroom floor
row.visual_description: Small bath rug on floor with visibly curled edges, no rubber backing, or lying on smooth tile without anchoring.
detection_cues: rug bunched or sliding on tile
recommended_fix: Remove or replace with non-skid backed rug
row.post_op_modifier: A sliding rug can catch walker feet or cause a trip during transfer to/from bathroom, high risk post-op.
row.citation: Small bath rugs that slide or have curled edges should be removed, or replaced with rugs that have a non-skid backing.

row.name: Handrail loose, short, or not full length
row.visual_description: Handrail appears wobbly, detached at a bracket, or terminates before reaching the top/bottom of the stairs.
detection_cues: visible gap between rail and wall bracket
recommended_fix: Firmly reattach or extend handrail to run full length of stairs
row.post_op_modifier: An unstable or short rail can fail exactly when a walker user needs support most, e.g. near top or bottom step.
row.citation: Handrails should be firmly attached on both sides of the stairs and run the whole length of the stairway.

row.name: No night light on path to bathroom
row.visual_description: Hallway or bathroom entry path is dark with no visible night light or illuminated fixture.
detection_cues: no glow from outlet or wall light
recommended_fix: Install plug-in or motion-sensor night light along path to bathroom
row.post_op_modifier: Nighttime walker navigation is riskier when vision is impaired, increasing fall risk after hip surgery.
row.citation: Keep a night light on so the path to the bathroom is visible at night.

row.name: Loose or torn stair carpet
row.visual_description: Carpet on stair treads is wrinkled, bulging, torn, or not tacked down flush to the step edge.
detection_cues: visible carpet lip or fold at step edge
recommended_fix: Remove loose carpet or re-tack it securely to each step
row.post_op_modifier: A loose carpet edge can catch a walker leg or foot, causing a fall with high fracture-recurrence risk.
row.citation: Carpet on the stairs must be tight to every step; remove it or tack it down if it is loose or torn.

row.name: Low toilet seat without raised seat or frame
row.visual_description: Standard-height toilet with no raised seat attachment or safety frame visible around it.
detection_cues: low seat height relative to floor
no frame with armrests around bowl
recommended_fix: Add raised toilet seat or toilet safety frame
row.post_op_modifier: Deep hip flexion required to sit on a low seat can violate post-op hip precautions and cause dislocation risk.
row.citation: A raised toilet seat or a toilet safety frame makes it easier to sit and stand, especially after hip surgery.

plan.prompt: a pair of sneakers left resting on the lower stair tread, casting a soft shadow, matching the warm wood tone and lighting of the staircase
bare white fiberglass shower wall with no grab bars, smooth surface matching surrounding tub/shower enclosure
plan.search_prompt: stainless steel grab bars mounted on shower wall
